ENDORSEMENT TITLE:  Water Damage and Plumbing Systems Endorsement

This endorsement modifies the insurance provided under the Homeowners Policy
to which it is attached. It amends coverage for losses arising from water
damage originating from interior plumbing, fixtures, and water supply systems
within the insured dwelling and its attached structures.

SECTION I — SCOPE AND PURPOSE

This endorsement applies only to losses involving water that originates from
the plumbing, heating, air-conditioning, or automatic fire-protective sprinkler
systems within the dwelling premises. Coverage under this endorsement is
subject to the deductible stated on the Declarations page and is excess of any
applicable sub-limit shown in Schedule A of the base policy.

Where a loss involves both a covered water-damage peril and an excluded peril,
the Company shall pay only for the portion of the loss attributable to the
covered peril, determined on a reasonable and equitable basis.

SECTION II — DEFINITIONS

covered peril, determined on a reasonable and equitable basis.

SECTION II — DEFINITIONS

For purposes of this endorsement, the following definitions apply in addition
to those in the base policy:

(a) "Plumbing System" means all pipes, fittings, valves, fixtures, and
    appliances installed within the dwelling premises for the purpose of
    distributing water or removing waterborne waste, including but not limited
    to supply lines, drain lines, water heaters, dishwashers, and washing
    machines.

(b) "Sudden and Accidental Discharge" means a discharge or overflow of water
    that occurs abruptly and is neither expected nor intended by the insured.
    A burst pipe, a failed valve, or a ruptured supply hose constitutes a
    sudden and accidental discharge.

(c) "Gradual Seepage" means the slow, continuous, or repeated passage of water
    through cracks, joints, or porous surfaces over a period exceeding
    fourteen (14) calendar days, whether or not observable by the insured.

SECTION III — COVERAGE MODIFICATIONS

A. Coverage A — Dwelling. Water damage to the dwelling structure (walls,
   floors, ceilings, insulation, and built-in cabinetry) is covered when
   caused by a sudden and accidental discharge from the plumbing system,
   subject to a per-occurrence sub-limit of $50,000 unless a higher limit
   is shown on the Declarations page.

B. Coverage C — Personal Pro

sudden and accidental discharge from the plumbing system,
   subject to a per-occurrence sub-limit of $50,000 unless a higher limit
   is shown on the Declarations page.

B. Coverage C — Personal Property. Damage to personal property caused by a
   sudden and accidental discharge is covered up to the Coverage C limit,
   less the applicable deductible.

C. Reasonable Costs of Tear-Out. The Company will pay reasonable costs
   incurred to tear out and replace any part of the dwelling necessary to
   repair the plumbing system from which the water escaped, provided the
   discharge was sudden and accidental.

SECTION V — CONDITIONS

1. Duty to Mitigate. The insured shall take all reasonable steps to prevent
   further water damage after discovering a discharge, including shutting off
   the water supply and contacting a licensed plumber. Failure to mitigate may
   reduce the amount payable under this endorsement.

2. Documentation. The insured must provide photographic or video evidence of
   the damage and retain all replaced components for inspection by the
   Company's adjuster.

3. Coordination with Flood Policy. If the insured also maintains a separate
   flood insurance policy (e.g., NFIP or private flood), this endorsement
   does not duplicate flood coverage. Any amount payable under the flood

ENDORSEMENT TITLE:  Ordinance or Law Coverage Endorsement

This endorsement modifies the insurance provided under the Homeowners Policy
to which it is attached. It provides coverage for the increased costs an
insured may incur when repairing or rebuilding a damaged dwelling to comply
with current building codes, ordinances, or laws that were enacted after the
original construction of the dwelling.

SECTION I — SCOPE AND PURPOSE

Following a covered loss to the dwelling, the enforcement of building codes or
ordinances may require the insured to incur costs beyond the direct physical
damage. This endorsement provides three categories of additional coverage:

  (a) Coverage for the loss in value of the undamaged portion of the dwelling
      when a building ordinance requires demolition of the entire structure;
  (b) Coverage for the cost of demolishing and clearing the undamaged portion;
  (c) Coverage for the increased cost of construction to meet current codes.

The combined limit of liability fo

ructure;
  (b) Coverage for the cost of demolishing and clearing the undamaged portion;
  (c) Coverage for the increased cost of construction to meet current codes.

The combined limit of liability for all three categories shall not exceed the
Ordinance or Law Coverage Limit stated on the Declarations page, or 10% of
the Coverage A limit, whichever is greater.

SECTION II — DEFINITIONS

(a) "Building Code" means any ordinance, law, or regulation governing the
    construction, repair, renovation, or demolition of a building, including
    zoning laws, environmental regulations, and accessibility standards such
    as the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA).

(b) "Functionally Equivalent" means construction that serves the same purpose
    and provides the same utility as the original, using currently available
    materials and methods, even if such materials differ from those originally
    used.

(c) "Increased Cost of Construction" means the additional expense, beyond
    the cost of repairing or replacing the damaged portion, required to bring
    the repaired or rebuilt dwelling into compliance with current building
    codes.

SECTION III — COVERAGE MODIFICATIONS

A. Loss of Undamaged Portion. If a building code requires the demolition of
   the undamaged portion of the dwelling, the Company will pay for the loss
   in value of that undamaged portion, calculated as the replacement cost of
   the undamaged portion less its salvage value.

B. Demolition and Clearing Cos

welling, the Company will pay for the loss
   in value of that undamaged portion, calculated as the replacement cost of
   the undamaged portion less its salvage value.

B. Demolition and Clearing Costs. The Company will pay the reasonable costs
   of demolishing and clearing the site of the undamaged portion, including
   debris removal and disposal fees required by environmental regulations.

C. Increased Construction Costs. The Company will pay the additional cost to
   repair, rebuild, or construct the dwelling using methods and materials
   required by the current building code, above the cost of restoring the
   dwelling to its pre-loss condition. This includes upgrades to electrical,
   plumbing, insulation, and structural systems mandated by code.

SECTION V — CONDITIONS

1. Duty to Comply. The insured must make a good-faith effort to comply with
   all applicable building codes when repairing or rebuilding. If the insured
   elects not to rebuild, the Company shall pay the lesser of the increased
   cost of construction or the actual cash value of the loss.

2. Time Limit for Construction. Increased construction costs are covered only
   if construction begins within two (2) years of the date of the covered loss
   and is completed within a reasonable time thereafter.

3. Prior Violations. This endorsement does not cover costs to correct
   pre-existing code violations that existed before the date of the covered
   loss.

4. Multiple Codes. Where multiple building codes apply, the Company will pay
   the cost to meet the most restrictive applica

ting code violations that existed before the date of the covered
   loss.

4. Multiple Codes. Where multiple building codes apply, the Company will pay
   the cost to meet the most restrictive applicable code, but not to exceed

ENDORSEMENT TITLE:  Earth Movement Endorsement

This endorsement modifies the insurance provided under the Homeowners Policy
to which it is attached. It provides limited coverage for direct physical
loss to the dwelling and personal property caused by earth movement,
subject to the terms, exclusions, and conditions stated below.

SECTION I — SCOPE AND PURPOSE

Earth movement includes, but is not limited to, earthquake, landslide,
mudflow, mudslide, sinkhole collapse, subsidence, and any other earth
movement (including earth movement resulting from volcanic activity).
Coverage under this endorsement is subject to a separate Earth Movement
Deductible stated on the Declarations page, expressed as a percentage
of the Coverage A limit (typically 5%, 10%, or 15%).

This endorsement does not replace or duplicate earthquake coverage provided
under a standalone earthquake policy. If the insured maintains a separate
earthquake policy, coverage under this endorsement is excess of amounts
payable under that p

cate earthquake coverage provided
under a standalone earthquake policy. If the insured maintains a separate
earthquake policy, coverage under this endorsement is excess of amounts
payable under that policy.

SECTION II — DEFINITIONS

(a) "Earth Movement" means any natural or human-caused shifting, settling,
    cracking, sinking, rising, or lateral displacement of earth, soil, or
    rock, whether sudden or gradual.

(b) "Sinkhole Collapse" means the sudden settlement or collapse of earth
    into a subsurface void created by the dissolution of underlying limestone
    or other soluble rock (karst geology).

(c) "Zone A Karst Terrain" means geographic areas identified by the state
    geological survey as having a high probability of sinkhole activity due
    to the presence of carbonate bedrock at shallow depth. The insured
    Declarations page identifies whether the dwelling premises are located
    in Zone A.

(d) "Mine Subsidence" means lateral or vertical ground movement caused by
    the collapse of man-made underground mines, including coal mines,
    limestone quarries, and salt mines.

SECTION III — COVERAGE MODIFICATIONS

A. Coverage A — Dwelling. Direct physical loss to the dwelling caused by
   earth movement is covered up to the Coverage A limit, less the Earth
   Movement Deductible. The Company will pay the cost to repair or replace
   the damaged dwelling at replacement cost, provided the insured rebuilds
   on the same premises.

B. Coverage B — Other Struct

ovement Deductible. The Company will pay the cost to repair or replace
   the damaged dwelling at replacement cost, provided the insured rebuilds
   on the same premises.

B. Coverage B — Other Structures. Loss to other structures (detached garages,
   fences, retaining walls) caused by earth movement is covered up to the
   Coverage B limit, less the Earth Movement Deductible.

C. Coverage C — Personal Property. Loss to personal property caused by earth
   movement is covered at actual cash value, unless the insured has
   purchased the Replacement Cost on Personal Property endorsement.

D. Additional Living Expense. If earth movement renders the dwelling
   uninhabitable, the Company will pay additional living expenses under
   Coverage D for up to twelve (12) months.

SECTION V — CONDITIONS

1. Inspection Requirement. After any earth movement event, the insured must
   arrange for a structural inspection by a licensed engineer within sixty
   (60) days. The Company may deny the claim if the insured fails t

irement. After any earth movement event, the insured must
   arrange for a structural inspection by a licensed engineer within sixty

   the inspection.

2. Multiple Events. If multiple earth movement events occur within a
   seventy-two (72) hour period, they shall be treated as a single
   occurrence for purposes of the deductible.

3. Land Stabilization. The Company will pay reasonable costs of land
   stabilization (e.g., grouting, underpinning) to prevent further damage
   to the dwelling, up to $25,000 per occurrence.

4. Government-Ordered Evacuation. If a governmental authority orders
   evacuation of the dwelling due to imminent earth movement, the Company
   will pay additional living expenses under Coverage D beginning on the
   date of the evacuation order.

ENDORSEMENT TITLE:  Home Business Property Endorsement

This endorsement modifies the insurance provided under the Homeowners Policy
to which it is attached. It extends Coverage C (Personal Property) to include
business property used in a home-based business operated by the insured on
the dwelling premises, subject to the terms, exclusions, and conditions
stated below.

SECTION I — SCOPE AND PURPOSE

The standard Homeowners Policy limits coverage for business property on the
dwelling premises to $2,500. This endorsement increases that limit to the
Home Business Property Limit stated on the Declarations page (typically
$10,000, $25,000, or $50,000) and broadens covered perils for qualifying
business property.

Qualifying business property includes furniture, equipment, supplies, and
inventory used primarily in the insured's home-based business. It does not
include motor vehicles, aircraft, watercraft, or property insured under a
separate commercial policy.

SECTION II — DEFINITIONS

(a) "Home-Base

marily in the insured's home-based business. It does not
include motor vehicles, aircraft, watercraft, or property insured under a
separate commercial policy.

SECTION II — DEFINITIONS

(a) "Home-Based Business" means a business operated by the named insured or
    a resident relative primarily on the dwelling premises, with gross annual
    revenue not exceeding $250,000. Businesses exceeding this threshold
    require a separate commercial property policy.

(b) "Business Property" means tangible property owned by the insured and
    used primarily for business purposes, including computers, printers,
    office furniture, tools, professional instruments, and inventory held
    for sale.

(c) "Electronic Data" means information, facts, or programs stored as or on,
    created or used on, or transmitted to or from computer software, including
    systems and applications software, hard or floppy disks, CD-ROMs, tapes,
    drives, cells, data processing devices, or any other media which are used
    with electronically controlled equipment.

SECTION III — COVERAGE MODIFICATIONS

A. Increased Business Property Limit. Coverage C is amended to provide
   coverage for business property on the dwelling premises up to the Home
   Business Property Limit, less the policy deductible.

B. Business Property in Transit. Business property in transit between the
   dwelling premises and a temporary business location (e.g., trade show,
   client site) is covered up to $5,000 per occurrence.

Business Property in Transit. Business property in transit between the

C. Accounts Receivable. The Company will pay up to $10,000 for loss of

D. Business Income Interruption. If a covered peril renders the business
   property unusable, the Company will pay lost business income for up to
   thirty (30) days, subject to a sub-limit of $5,000.

ENDORSEMENT TITLE:  Equipment Breakdown Endorsement

This endorsement modifies the insurance provided under the Dwelling Fire
Policy to which it is attached. It provides coverage for direct physical
loss caused by the sudden and accidental breakdown of covered equipment
located on the insured premises, subject to the terms, exclusions, and
conditions stated below.

SECTION I — SCOPE AND PURPOSE

Standard property policies exclude loss caused by mechanical or electrical
breakdown of equipment. This endorsement restores coverage for such losses
when the breakdown is sudden and accidental, as defined herein. Coverage
applies to permanently installed equipment serving the insured dwelling,
including heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems,
electrical panels, water heaters, well pumps, and built-in appliances.

The Equipment Breakdown Coverage Limit is equal to the Coverage A limit
unless a separate limit is shown on the Declarations page. The deductible
applicable to this end

umps, and built-in appliances.

The Equipment Breakdown Coverage Limit is equal to the Coverage A limit
unless a separate limit is shown on the Declarations page. The deductible
applicable to this endorsement is $500 or the policy deductible, whichever
is greater.

SECTION II — DEFINITIONS

(a) "Covered Equipment" means any equipment listed on the Equipment Schedule
    attached to this endorsement, or if no schedule is attached, any
    permanently installed mechanical or electrical equipment that serves
    the dwelling and is owned by the insured. Portable or plug-in appliances
    (e.g., window air-conditioning units, portable heaters, kitchen counter
    appliances) are not covered equipment unless specifically scheduled.

(b) "Breakdown" means the sudden and accidental failure of covered equipment
    that manifests as physical damage requiring repair or replacement. A
    breakdown must originate within the equipment itself and must not result
    from an external cause such as fire, lightning, windstorm, or vandalism
    (which are covered under the base policy).

(c) "Expediting Expenses" means reasonable extra costs to make temporary
    repairs or to expedite permanent repairs, including overtime labor and
    express shipping of replacement parts.

SECTION III — COVERAGE MODIFICATIONS

A. Equipment Repair or Replacement. The Company will pay the cost to repair
   or replace covered equipment that has suffered a breakdown, at replacement
   cost, less the applicabl

A. Equipment Repair or Replacement. The Company will pay the cost to repair
   or replace covered equipment that has suffered a breakdown, at replacement
   cost, less the applicable deductible.

B. Spoilage Coverage. If a breakdown of refrigeration or climate-control
   equipment causes spoilage of perishable goods (e.g., food, medicine),
   the Company will pay up to $2,500 per occurrence for spoiled goods.

C. Expediting Expenses. The Company will pay expediting expenses up to
   $5,000 per occurrence to restore the function of the covered equipment
   as quickly as possible.

D. Utility Interruption. If a breakdown at a utility provider's facility
   causes a covered equipment breakdown at the insured premises, coverage
   applies as if the breakdown occurred on-premises, provided the utility
   interruption lasts more than twenty-four (24) hours.

ENDORSEMENT TITLE:  Scheduled Personal Property Endorsement

This endorsement modifies the insurance provided under the Dwelling Fire
Policy to which it is attached. It provides broader coverage and agreed-value
protection for specifically listed (scheduled) personal property items of
high value, including jewelry, fine art, musical instruments, firearms,
collectibles, and electronic equipment.

SECTION I — SCOPE AND PURPOSE

The standard policy limits coverage for certain categories of personal
property (e.g., jewelry is limited to $1,500 for theft). This endorsement
removes those sub-limits for items individually listed and appraised on the
Personal Property Schedule attached to the Declarations page.

Scheduled items are covered on an open-perils, agreed-value basis. The
Company will pay the agreed value stated on the schedule for a total loss,
or the cost of repair or replacement for a partial loss, without application
of depreciation.

Coverage applies worldwide — scheduled items are covered whether on the
dwelling premises, in transit, or at any other location, subject to the
exclusions below.

SECTION II — DEFINITIONS

(a) "Scheduled Item" means an article of personal property individually
    listed by description and appraised value on the Personal Property
    Schedule. Each item must be supported by a professional appraisal or
    purchase receipt dated within three (3) years of the policy effective
    date or most recent renewal.

(b) "Agreed Value" means the dollar amount stated on the Personal Property
    Schedule for each scheduled item, as agreed between the insured and the
    Company at the time of scheduling. The agreed value is the maximum the
    Company will pay for a total loss of that item.

(c) "Mysterious Disappearance" means the vanishing of an item of personal
    property from a known location under unexplained circumstances, without
    evidence of a specific peril such as theft, fire, or windstorm.

(d) "Pair or Set" means two or more items that have a combined value
    exceeding the sum of their individual values due to their association
    with each other (e.g., a matched pair of earrings, a complete set of
    china, a series of prints).

SECTION III — COVERAGE MODIFICATIONS

A. Agreed-Value Coverage. For each scheduled item, the Company will pay up
   to the agreed value for a total loss. No deductible applies to scheduled
   items unless otherwise stated on the Declarations page.

B. Partial Loss. For partial damage to a scheduled item, the Company will
   pay the lesser of the cost to restore the item to its pre-loss condition
   or the agreed value.

C. Newly Acquired Items. Items acquired after the policy inception are
   automatically covered for up to ninety (90) days at a maximum of $25,000
   per item, provided the insured reports the item and provides an appraisal
   within the ninety-day period.

D. Worldwide Coverage. Scheduled items are covered at any location worldwide.
   Coverage for items temporarily outside the United States or Canada is
   limited to ninety (90) consecutive days per trip.
